questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Going outside of Europe.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Easy. The University sends a lot of e-mails before arriving, and there are services on campus that help new international students with arrival, accommodation, studying in Canada etc.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: You receive a lot of assistance. Mostly through e-mail. Going to the international services at campus in-person is also a great help, they will tell you where to go, what to do, and how to get started with studying in Canada.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Several on-campus housing options. You could share an apartment with roommates, or live in a dorm with your own bathroom and shared kitchen.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: The University provides a meal plan for students but it is quite expensive. You can purchase meal tickets if you don't want to buy a full meal plan, but overall this is not worth the price. Cooking for yourself is cheaper.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It's a great opportunity to meet new people and make friends. I highly recommend it. The rooms are not amazing, and it is quite expensive, but for the experience, I think it is worth it. You have to bring everything. Kitchen utensils, cleaning, etc., are not provided.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You register via the university's own portal (BearTracks).

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You receive e-mails prior to registration that explain how to register with videos showing the process / what to do. There is a lot of information on the University of Alberta website, and you can see course descriptions prior to registering. The course descriptions are not always very good though.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Successful. As an exchange student, you do not have first priority. This goes to the domestic students. However, a lot of students drop courses, so spots become available at the beginning of the term, and you can easily get the courses you want after this period. I got all the courses I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Save the courses you want and pay attention to your e-mail. It will say if someone drops the course, and then you can register if you are fast enough. Plan your courses so you don't have a heavy workload throughout the semester.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: You take undergraduate (BA) courses, even as a master's student. The level is not very different from Denmark. Same amount of reading. There are midterms, which is not common in Danish programs or law courses. Exams are shorter. Depending on the course, the exams can be very similar to Danish law exams (fact-patterns) or very different (multiple choice). A lot of work throughout the semester with assignments that count towards your grade. Participation also matters in some courses so your grade is not only based on a final exam. It can be hard to get used to the common-law system at first.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The courses are much more seminar based. Less group work or discussion, but this differs from every course. The professor will usually spend most of class presenting with no breaks.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Public International Law, Administrative Law, Environmental Law, Canadian Human Rights Law, Professionalism & Ethics

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Public International Law and Canadian Human Rights Law! Both are very good courses with great professors.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Mandatory health care from the University (200 CAD).

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Housing is expensive. Eating out is cheaper compared to Denmark.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Several clubs to join. Most of them promote themselves during the first week of the term. A lot of sports clubs. Gym is free and very good. All of the university's sports games are free to attend as a student (hockey, basketball etc.)

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go to a hockey game. Go skiing. Explore campus and the city.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go out. A lot of students go to downtown in the weekends. See the nature. Visit the big cities like Toronto, Vancouver, Montreal, etc. All are very good.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy. Meet other international students, they all want to make friends. Canadians are very friendly and enjoy talking.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Be social. Just talk to people. In residence, at class, and around campus. It is not hard to make friends as long as you try.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: There is a homeless crisis in Canada. You will see more homeless people on the streets than you do in Denmark. They are mostly harmless, but it is something you have to get used to.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The friendliness. Canadians are very open, talkative, and nice people. They enjoy smalltalk.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Live on campus - this is the best way to meet people and have a good experience. 
Be social and outgoing. Join clubs. Do sports. 
Travel if you can and explore Canada.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Dress well. It gets cold.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting people from all over the world. Traveling.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Getting used to the common law system.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
